proof_summary: Prime valuations of the numerator and denominator are expanded as \(\sum_i\lfloor n/p^i\rfloor^2\) and \(\sum_i\sum_k k\lfloor\lfloor n/p^i\rfloor/k\rfloor\), respectively; the termwise bound \(\sum_k k\lfloor M/k\rfloor\le M^2\) proves exact divisibility and permits valuation subtraction. When passing from \(t\) to \(t+1\) with \(p\nmid t+1\), every newly introduced gcd and every new factorial factor has zero \(p\)-valuation, so the quotient valuation is unchanged; iterating this through the integers strictly between consecutive multiples of \(p\) gives the result.
